To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) sunshine duration records can be used to study long-term changes in atmospheric turbidity, (2) the use of sunshine duration records to estimate aerosol-related magnities is feasible and (3) there is evidence that one cause for the changes observed in sunshine records involves variations in the atmospheric aerosol concentration.

(a) sunshine duration records are suitable for estimating aerosol-induced changes, especially when the data are processed using a sunrise and/or sunset filter; (b) the aerosol-induced change in sunshine duration is mainly related to the aerosol loading; and (c) sunshine duration records may be used to estimate the aerosol-related magnitues such as turbidity.
the sunshine duration signal is a good proxy of aerosol changes in the atmosphere.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of the signal recorded in the time series of sunshine duration as an index of changes in atmospheric aerosol concentrations.
the use of sunshine duration records for detecting and quantifying aerosol-induced changes.
the use of sunshine duration records to estimate changes in atmospheric turbidity, and the present review provides a useful reference for researchers interested in this topic.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

sunshine duration records are a suitable tool for monitoring changes in atmospheric aerosol concentrations, especially in the case of long-term studies, but further studies are needed to confirm the reliability and validity of such a conclusion.
, in spite of the limitations and uncertainties of sunshine duration records, they are a valuable source of information for the reconstruction of past changes in atmospheric aerosol concentrations.
sunshine duration records are suitable for the study of aerosol-induced variations, although they are not a perfect tool.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
sunshine duration is an important and valuable tool in the study of aerosol-induced variations in the Earth's radiative budget.
sunshine duration records are a valuable source of information about the long-term changes in atmospheric turbidity, and therefore, they should be considered in climate studies.
, despite the many difficulties involved, sunshine duration records are a potentially useful source of information on changes in atmospheric aerosol concentration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sunshine duration records are a valuable source of information on the atmospheric turbidity caused by aerosols.

sunshine duration series may be used as a proxy for atmospheric turbidity, and that the use of such series may provide a means of detecting changes in atmospheric turbidity induced over the long term by anthropogenic aerosols.

, despite the fact that the signal of aerosol-related changes in sunshine duration is weak and difficult to isolate, the available evidence suggests that it is possible to obtain reliable estimates of the aerosol-related component of the sunshine record, and that the information thus obtained is valuable for climate research.
